Hi! I'm Pia Deshpande — a PhD Candidate in the [Travers Department of Political Science](https://polisci.berkeley.edu/) at UC Berkeley. I have a particular interest in `how social media shapes American politics`. 

To that end, I am currently analyzing the results of a large field experiment (n = 2,148) I ran with [Aaron Pope](https://aaron-pope.github.io/), a PhD Candidate in Social Data Science at the University of Copenhagen. Pairing experimental evidence with digital trace data (over 130 million video exposures collected with 50 million _unique_ URLS across watch histories), we examine what deactivating TikTok for one month may do to Americans' political beliefs and well-being. With the wealth of watch history data at our disposal, we have also set out to describe the political landscape of the platform our participants engage with, with a specific eye to contact that blends entertainment and politics. Beyond this project, I am interested in how the internet changes (or does not change) people's ability to engage in politics.

Prior to starting my PhD at Berkeley, I was a pre-doctoral researcher at the [Cooperative Election Study (CES)](https://tischcollege.tufts.edu/research-faculty/research-centers/cooperative-election-study) and a research assistant at the [MIT Election Lab](https://electionlab.mit.edu/). I also worked as a data journalist for the Associated Press during the 2020 election, and interned at CNN International in Hong Kong and POLITICO in D.C. In 2020, I earned a B.A. in Political Science from Columbia University. 

Though I am not a journalist anymore, I continue to write for non-academic venues as a researcher. So far, I have published in *The Monkey Cage* and *Lawfare.*

During my time with the CES, I wrote tutorials for my students on how to use R. I wrote these tutorials before I even began graduate school, so I take only tenuous responsibility for the prose they contain. You can find them under `tutorials` .

You can contact me at `pia_deshpande[at]berkeley[dot]edu`.
